subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group chats get first-class opt-in dynamic per-sender agents, or should sender-scoped group sessions plus explicit subagent/thread commands remain the supported isolation model?
rationale: The remaining work changes product semantics and security boundaries across Feishu routing, config writes, memory visibility, subagent lifecycle, and group administration; source inspection shows the current code intentionally stops at DM dynamic agents plus group session scopes.

options.title: Design opt-in group-sender dynamic agents
options.body: Add a Feishu-owned opt-in mode with private/shared memory namespaces, admin authorization, lifecycle limits, and compatibility with existing groupSessionScope and bindings.

options.title: Keep current session isolation only
options.body: Close or defer automatic group subagents and document group_sender/group_topic_sender plus explicit subagent/thread commands as the supported model.

options.title: Split prerequisite APIs first
options.body: Keep this issue as an umbrella while separate issues define the needed memory, lifecycle, and channel admin contracts before implementation.

recommendation.title: Design opt-in group-sender dynamic agents
recommendation.body: Add a Feishu-owned opt-in mode with private/shared memory namespaces, admin authorization, lifecycle limits, and compatibility with existing groupSessionScope and bindings.

likelyOwner.reason: Current line history and recent Feishu routing work make vincentkoc the strongest available owner for deciding the channel-specific shape with adjacent owners reviewing security/session contracts.
